result.narrative:
Halberg Textiles GmbH is carrying one invoice 40 days past due (INV000220, €55,300) alongside five other open invoices with client CL01. Total open exposure is around €527,100 against a granted limit of €440,000, so the buyer is already over limit. There is no settled payment history at all — the trend flag reads "insufficient_history" — so the 40 DPD reading is a point-in-time snapshot with no behavioural track record behind it. The only news on file is a 2025-10-20 report that the Bielefeld unit moved from three shifts to one on weak order inflow; the company called it a "temporary realignment of production".

The score is 42.7, inside the Watch band of 35.0 to 60.0, with a PD of 0.3267. Payment does almost all the work: 0.65 x 60.0 (payment, 40 DPD) gives a weighted 39.0, while the news contributes a raw 10.5 decayed over 340 days for a weighted 3.7. The adjudicator agreed with the band but attached caveats: the formula scores only days past due and is blind both to the over-limit position across six open invoices and to the absence of any settlement history. They also noted the news rests on two anonymous sources and a former employee, and flagged an unexplained discrepancy in the age_days used for decay (small, and working against the buyer). Treat 42.7 as a caveated reading rather than a comfortable mid-Watch one.

The recommended action for Adlerhof Trade Credit (CL01, LIM0006) is FREEZE: the limit stays at €440,000 with no change, because the buyer already owes €527,100 — at or above the limit, so there is nothing left to cut. Expected loss is unchanged at €116,436 before and after, and PD of 0.3267 sits above the 0.25 target; the maximum liability constraint does not bind. The practical lever here is collection of the overdue €55,300 and refusing further shipment above the granted line, not a limit reduction. The credit limit was last reviewed in Nov 2024 and looks stale against current exposure — worth a fresh review alongside this decision.

To move Halberg out of Watch the score needs to fall 7.7 points below 35.0, which means clearing the 40 DPD arrears; news alone does not hold the band, and the capacity-cut item decays on a 365-day half-life so it will keep fading on its own. Bringing open exposure back under the €440,000 limit and building a run of settled invoices would give the trend flag something to work with and turn the current reading into an assessable pattern. Going the other way, 54 DPD on the worst line would carry the score to the 60.0 High Risk threshold, 17.3 points above where it sits now.

judgement.bottom_line: Hold the €440,000 limit for Adlerhof Trade Credit as a FREEZE — the buyer already owes €527,100, so there is nothing left to cut. The adjudicator agreed with the Watch band but caveated it: the 42.7 score reflects only the 40 DPD figure and ignores the over-limit position and the complete absence of settled payment history.
